body.content: Key insight: the main threat to minimum triangle area is collinear or near-collinear triples. A pure grid has many collinear triples (same row or column). Solutions must either: (1) use a perturbed grid where no three points share a line, (2) use a triangular lattice which naturally avoids collinearity, or (3) use an irregular but well-separated arrangement. The triangular lattice is promising because it maximizes minimum pairwise distance for a given density, and larger pairwise distances generally imply larger triangle areas.
body.why_keep_this: This insight guides which constructions to try and which to avoid.
